reading.body:
CyrusOne Lewisville DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet of technical space. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common baseline for general-purpose colocation, this capacity could host roughly 300 racks. At higher densities typical of AI training, such as 150 kW per rack, the same power budget would support approximately 80 racks of accelerator infrastructure. The campus ranks twelfth among the nineteen facilities in Texas with published power capacity.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS compliance, HIPAA eligibility, ISO 27001 information security, FISMA compliance for federal systems, SSAE 16 Type II audit standards, and TIA-942 data center tier classification. These certifications indicate the campus can host regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, government, and security-sensitive domains.

Lewisville DFW2 represents 2.5 percent of Texas's published 475 MW of data center IT capacity. Texas has 133 mapped data center sites, but only nineteen publish power figures, making detailed comparison difficult. The facility's power envelope places it below the scale threshold for large-scale AI training clusters, which typically require 50+ MW per campus in current deployments.
